title: Show environment-specific chrome
goal: Mark test environments and show the controls intended for each renderer.

selectionNotes: Server/client environments; case-insensitive include/exclude; not access control.

language.reason: Declared canonical sample mode; the component does not require novel C# syntax.
language.name: C#

constraints: Include and Exclude are comma-separated names with trimming, empty-entry removal and ordinal case-insensitive matching. Exclude wins. Missing/whitespace Include permits content unless excluded. A list with no valid include names acts as unspecified for a nonempty environment.

EnvironmentView hides presentation only. Browser environment values and client assets are public and alterable. Hidden chrome is not authorization: authenticate and authorize every protected operation on the server.

An empty/whitespace current environment renders only when both Include and Exclude are unspecified/whitespace (source-reviewed boundary). Server prerender and later browser rendering can have different environments. This example disables browser prerender so each observation has one renderer.

No .NET 10 EnvironmentView backport or older-target package route is claimed. Use the supported older service/conditional comparison. Auto, Hybrid, AOT and GA artifacts were not executed; no new .NET 10 foundation edition is introduced.

prerequisites: Use the complete Host/Client projects, explicit Razor imports, namespaces, document, CSS and boot JavaScript below. Actual baseline: SDK 11.0.100-rc.2.26504.105, runtime/packages 11.0.0-rc.2.26504.105, C# 15. No wasm-tools workload or AOT is required; WasmBuildNative=false.

WebApplication supplies server IHostEnvironment. WebAssemblyHostBuilder registers its real browser environment and IHostEnvironment adapter. The browser demonstration defaults to Review independently of the server; the query switch is public test setup only.
